title: Inspect and extend: Make and interpret GitHub API requests
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/github.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve fetch client, request paths, headers, response mapping, githuberror, and rate-limit headers.
problem: An HTTP client sends a request and turns a response into a useful shape. Trace URL construction and response handling, then inspect how API errors and rate-limit metadata are represented. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/github.ts` and the related project files: src/github.ts; test/github.test.ts.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to fetch client, request paths, headers, response mapping, githuberror, and rate-limit headers.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Authentication, token storage, pagination breadth, and current provider quotas need review before production use.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: An HTTP client sends a request and turns a response into a useful shape. Trace URL construction and response handling, then inspect how API errors and rate-limit metadata are represented.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/github.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
